verses.1: The Philistines gathered their armies for battle and assembled at Socoh in Judah. They camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes Dammim.
verses.2: Israel and Saul gathered and camped in the Valley of Elah, arranging themselves for battle against the Philistines.
verses.3: The Philistines stood on one hillside and Israel on the other, with the valley between them.
verses.4: A warrior from the Philistine ranks came out—his name was Goliath, from Gath. He was six cubits and a span tall.
verses.5: He had a bronze helmet on his head and wore a bronze coat of armor weighing five thousand shekels of bronze.
verses.6: He had bronze shin guards and a bronze sword between his shoulders.
verses.7: His spear shaft was like a weaver’s rod, and the spearhead weighed six hundred shekels of iron. A shield bearer walked ahead of him.
verses.8: He stood and called out to the Israelite ranks, saying, "Why do you come out to prepare for battle? Am I not the Philistine and you the servants of Saul? Choose a man and let him come down to me.
verses.9: If he is able to fight with me and strike me down, we will be your servants. But if I am able to overcome him and strike him down, you will be our servants and will serve us."
verses.10: Goliath said, "I have defied the ranks of Israel today. Give me a man, and we will fight each other."
verses.11: When Saul and all Israel heard the words of the Philistine, they were terrified and greatly afraid.
verses.12: David, the son of a man from Bethlehem in Judah, whose name was Jesse, had eight sons. Jesse was an old man in the days of Saul, respected among the people.
verses.13: The three eldest sons of Jesse had gone to follow Saul to the war: the name of the eldest was Eliab, the second Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
verses.14: David was the youngest, and the three older brothers had gone with Saul.
verses.15: David used to travel back and forth from Saul to tend his father's sheep in Bethlehem.
verses.16: The Philistine came out morning and evening for forty days.
verses.17: Jesse said to David his son, "Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves and go to your brothers who are at the camp.
verses.18: Also, take these ten cheeses of dried curds to the commander of a thousand and ask your brothers about their well-being and bring back their pledge."
verses.19: And Saul and they and all the men of Israel were in the Valley of Elah fighting with the Philistines.
verses.20: David rose early in the morning and left the sheep with a shepherd. He took the supplies and went to the camp and met the returning soldiers coming from the battle.
verses.21: Israel and the Philistines had arranged their ranks to face each other.
verses.22: David left his supplies with the guardian of the equipment and ran to the battle line and greeted his brothers.
verses.23: While he was speaking with them, the Benjamite warrior came up—Goliath the Philistine, from the ranks of the Philistines—and spoke as he always did. David heard it.
verses.24: All the men of Israel saw the man and fled from him, greatly afraid.
verses.25: One man of Israel said, "Have you seen this man who comes up? He comes to defy Israel. If the man who strikes him down will be rich with the riches of the king, the king will give him his daughter and make his father's house free in Israel."
verses.26: David said to the men who stood with him, "What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine who defies the ranks of the living God?"
verses.27: The people repeated to David the same words, "This will be done for the man who strikes him down."
verses.28: David's older brother Eliab heard him speaking to the men and became angry with David and said, "Why have you come down here? And whom have you left in charge of the few sheep? I know your arrogance and the evil of your heart, for you have come to see the battle."
verses.29: David replied, "What have I done now? Was it not just a word?"
verses.30: He turned away from his brother and spoke to the others in the same way. The people still gave him the same answer as before.
verses.31: The words David spoke were heard, and they were reported to Saul. He sent for him.
verses.32: David said to Saul, "Let not the heart of any man fall because of him. Your servant will go and fight this Philistine."
verses.33: Saul said to David, "You are not able to go out to fight this Philistine to fight with him, for you are just a boy, and he is a man of war from his youth."
verses.34: David said to Saul, "Your servant has been the shepherd for his father's sheep. When a lion or a bear came and took a lamb from the flock,
verses.35: I went after it, struck it down, and rescued the lamb from its mouth. If it turned on me, I seized it by the beard, struck it down, and killed it.
verses.36: I have struck both the lion and the bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them. For he has defied the ranks of the living God."
verses.37: David said, "The Lord who rescued me from the hand of the lion and the hand of the bear will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine." Saul said to David, "Go! May the Lord be with you."
verses.38: Saul clothed David with his own tunic and placed a bronze helmet on his head and put a coat of armor on him.
verses.39: David fastened the sword over his tunic and tried to walk in them, but he could not, for he had not tested them. So David removed them.
verses.40: He took his staff in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the stream, put them in his shepherd’s bag, and took his sling in his hand. Then he approached the Philistine.
verses.41: The Philistine advanced and drew near to David, with the shield bearer in front of him.
verses.42: The Philistine looked at David and despised him, for he was just a boy and handsome in appearance.
verses.43: The Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog that you come against me with sticks?" Then the Philistine cursed David in his gods.
verses.44: He said to David, "Come here, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field."
verses.45: David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with sword and spear and shield, but I come to you in the name of the Lord of Hosts, the God of the ranks of Israel, whom you have defied.
verses.46: Today the Lord will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down and cut off your head. And I will give the dead bodies of the Philistine camp this day to the birds of the sky and to the wild animals, and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.
verses.47: And all of this assembly will know that it is not by sword or spear that the Lord saves, for the battle is the Lord's, and He will give you into our hands."
verses.48: As the Philistine advanced to meet David, David ran quickly to the battle line to meet him.
verses.49: David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and slung it. The stone struck the Philistine's forehead, and it sank into him. He fell face down on the ground.
verses.50: David was stronger than the Philistine with the sling and stone, for he struck the Philistine and killed him. David had no sword in his hand.
verses.51: David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it from its sheath, and killed him. He cut off his head and the Philistines saw that their champion was dead and fled.
verses.52: The men of Israel and Judah rose and attacked and chased the Philistines to Gai until they reached the gates of Ekron. The Philistine dead fell along the road to the gates of Gath and Ekron.
verses.53: The Israelites returned from chasing the Philistines and plundered their camps.
verses.54: David took the Philistine's head and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put his weapons in his tent.
verses.55: When Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, "Whose son is this youth?" Abner replied, "As your life is, I do not know."
verses.56: The king said, "Ask me, whose son is this, this young man?"
verses.57: When David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the Philistine's head in his hand.
verses.58: Saul said to him, "Whose son are you, young man?" David answered, "I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."

notes:
Notes
- v. 5: "five thousand shekels of bronze" — the Hebrew uses "shekels of bronze" rather than "shekels of silver," reflecting the material used in the Philistine context.
- v. 42: "handsome in appearance" — the Hebrew uses "admoni" (reddish) and "yafeh mar'eh" (beautiful to see), which are translated to convey both physical features and general attractiveness.
- v. 58: "Jesse the Bethlehemite" — the Hebrew uses "beth lechemi" (from Bethlehem) to specify the origin of Jesse.
raw:
[1] The Philistines gathered their armies for battle and assembled at Socoh in Judah. They camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes Dammim.

[2] Israel and Saul gathered and camped in the Valley of Elah, arranging themselves for battle against the Philistines.

[3] The Philistines stood on one hillside and Israel on the other, with the valley between them.

[4] A warrior from the Philistine ranks came out—his name was Goliath, from Gath. He was six cubits and a span tall.

[5] He had a bronze helmet on his head and wore a bronze coat of armor weighing five thousand shekels of bronze.

[6] He had bronze shin guards and a bronze sword between his shoulders.

[7] His spear shaft was like a weaver’s rod, and the spearhead weighed six hundred shekels of iron. A shield bearer walked ahead of him.

[8] He stood and called out to the Israelite ranks, saying, "Why do you come out to prepare for battle? Am I not the Philistine and you the servants of Saul? Choose a man and let him come down to me.

[9] If he is able to fight with me and strike me down, we will be your servants. But if I am able to overcome him and strike him down, you will be our servants and will serve us."

[10] Goliath said, "I have defied the ranks of Israel today. Give me a man, and we will fight each other."

[11] When Saul and all Israel heard the words of the Philistine, they were terrified and greatly afraid.

[12] David, the son of a man from Bethlehem in Judah, whose name was Jesse, had eight sons. Jesse was an old man in the days of Saul, respected among the people.

[13] The three eldest sons of Jesse had gone to follow Saul to the war: the name of the eldest was Eliab, the second Abinadab, and the third Shammah.

[14] David was the youngest, and the three older brothers had gone with Saul.

[15] David used to travel back and forth from Saul to tend his father's sheep in Bethlehem.

[16] The Philistine came out morning and evening for forty days.

[17] Jesse said to David his son, "Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves and go to your brothers who are at the camp.

[18] Also, take these ten cheeses of dried curds to the commander of a thousand and ask your brothers about their well-being and bring back their pledge."

[19] And Saul and they and all the men of Israel were in the Valley of Elah fighting with the Philistines.

[20] David rose early in the morning and left the sheep with a shepherd. He took the supplies and went to the camp and met the returning soldiers coming from the battle.

[21] Israel and the Philistines had arranged their ranks to face each other.

[22] David left his supplies with the guardian of the equipment and ran to the battle line and greeted his brothers.

[23] While he was speaking with them, the Benjamite warrior came up—Goliath the Philistine, from the ranks of the Philistines—and spoke as he always did. David heard it.

[24] All the men of Israel saw the man and fled from him, greatly afraid.

[25] One man of Israel said, "Have you seen this man who comes up? He comes to defy Israel. If the man who strikes him down will be rich with the riches of the king, the king will give him his daughter and make his father's house free in Israel."

[26] David said to the men who stood with him, "What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine who defies the ranks of the living God?"

[27] The people repeated to David the same words, "This will be done for the man who strikes him down."

[28] David's older brother Eliab heard him speaking to the men and became angry with David and said, "Why have you come down here? And whom have you left in charge of the few sheep? I know your arrogance and the evil of your heart, for you have come to see the battle."

[29] David replied, "What have I done now? Was it not just a word?"

[30] He turned away from his brother and spoke to the others in the same way. The people still gave him the same answer as before.

[31] The words David spoke were heard, and they were reported to Saul. He sent for him.

[32] David said to Saul, "Let not the heart of any man fall because of him. Your servant will go and fight this Philistine."

[33] Saul said to David, "You are not able to go out to fight this Philistine to fight with him, for you are just a boy, and he is a man of war from his youth."

[34] David said to Saul, "Your servant has been the shepherd for his father's sheep. When a lion or a bear came and took a lamb from the flock,

[35] I went after it, struck it down, and rescued the lamb from its mouth. If it turned on me, I seized it by the beard, struck it down, and killed it.

[36] I have struck both the lion and the bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them. For he has defied the ranks of the living God."

[37] David said, "The Lord who rescued me from the hand of the lion and the hand of the bear will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine." Saul said to David, "Go! May the Lord be with you."

[38] Saul clothed David with his own tunic and placed a bronze helmet on his head and put a coat of armor on him.

[39] David fastened the sword over his tunic and tried to walk in them, but he could not, for he had not tested them. So David removed them.

[40] He took his staff in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the stream, put them in his shepherd’s bag, and took his sling in his hand. Then he approached the Philistine.

[41] The Philistine advanced and drew near to David, with the shield bearer in front of him.

[42] The Philistine looked at David and despised him, for he was just a boy and handsome in appearance.

[43] The Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog that you come against me with sticks?" Then the Philistine cursed David in his gods.

[44] He said to David, "Come here, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field."

[45] David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with sword and spear and shield, but I come to you in the name of the Lord of Hosts, the God of the ranks of Israel, whom you have defied.

[46] Today the Lord will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down and cut off your head. And I will give the dead bodies of the Philistine camp this day to the birds of the sky and to the wild animals, and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.

[47] And all of this assembly will know that it is not by sword or spear that the Lord saves, for the battle is the Lord's, and He will give you into our hands."

[48] As the Philistine advanced to meet David, David ran quickly to the battle line to meet him.

[49] David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and slung it. The stone struck the Philistine's forehead, and it sank into him. He fell face down on the ground.

[50] David was stronger than the Philistine with the sling and stone, for he struck the Philistine and killed him. David had no sword in his hand.

[51] David ran and stood over the Philistine, took his sword, drew it from its sheath, and killed him. He cut off his head and the Philistines saw that their champion was dead and fled.

[52] The men of Israel and Judah rose and attacked and chased the Philistines to Gai until they reached the gates of Ekron. The Philistine dead fell along the road to the gates of Gath and Ekron.

[53] The Israelites returned from chasing the Philistines and plundered their camps.

[54] David took the Philistine's head and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put his weapons in his tent.

[55] When Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, "Whose son is this youth?" Abner replied, "As your life is, I do not know."

[56] The king said, "Ask me, whose son is this, this young man?"

[57] When David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the Philistine's head in his hand.

[58] Saul said to him, "Whose son are you, young man?" David answered, "I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."

Notes
- v. 5: "five thousand shekels of bronze" — the Hebrew uses "shekels of bronze" rather than "shekels of silver," reflecting the material used in the Philistine context.
- v. 42: "handsome in appearance" — the Hebrew uses "admoni" (reddish) and "yafeh mar'eh" (beautiful to see), which are translated to convey both physical features and general attractiveness.
- v. 58: "Jesse the Bethlehemite" — the Hebrew uses "beth lechemi" (from Bethlehem) to specify the origin of Jesse.
